clue.text: Become smoother

blocks.note: first meaning: to suit or show off well, as a dress becomes its wearer
second meaning: more level, an adjective in the comparative

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one instruction, to grow smoother, but they split into a verb meaning 'suit' and a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour that suits you is said to do you favours in this way, and a more even surface is one with fewer bumps.

clue.text: Unpleasant bird noise

indicators.note: a noise is something heard, so we want a word that sounds like the bird

blocks.note: a fowl is a bird, especially a farmyard one

explanation.surface: A bird making a horrible racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty or disgusting, like a smell, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Engage in a race around short course

indicators.note: short means the word for course loses its final letter
the race goes around, enclosing the shortened course word

blocks.note: taken as written
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a racing course or track

explanation.surface: Someone signing up to compete in a race around a short circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' is the Isle of Man motorcycle event, the usual crossword shorthand; the shortened course word sits inside it, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone's interest or attention is to draw it towards you, which is this verb.

clue.text: Shortly it is going to become woven fabric

blocks.note: 'it will', shortened as people say it

explanation.surface: Something is about to be turned into cloth before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it means the phrase it is going, i.e. it will, is contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a cloth woven with diagonal parallel ribs, as in denim or gabardine.

clue.text: Restricted relationship with boy

blocks.note: a ratio is the relationship between two quantities
Ned, short for Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy kept on a tight rein in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relationship' suggests romance, but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or fuel handed out in limited fixed amounts, as in wartime, has been restricted this way.

clue.text: Haddock initially being mistaken for another fish

indicators.note: initially means we keep just the opening letter of the fish named first

blocks.note: first letter of the fish
erring means making a mistake, being wrong

explanation.surface: A haddock wrongly identified as a different fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a familiar silvery sea fish, so it is indeed another fish besides the haddock.

clue.text: Covering up corporal punishment

blocks.note: first meaning: concealing something
second meaning: a thrashing or beating

explanation.surface: Concealing the fact that a child was beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealment is keeping something out of sight, and a good thrashing is colloquially called a sound one of these.

clue.text: Cooked rook parts for Sunday dinner

indicators.note: something cooked is changed from its raw state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pieces of a rook, the black bird, prepared for the Sunday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A traditional British Sunday dinner is a roast joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This joint of pig meat is a classic example of the British Sunday roast lunch.

clue.text: Early? first of all is never in time, is always late!

indicators.note: first of all means take the opening letter of every following word

blocks.clueFragment: is never in time, is always late
blocks.note: opening letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A chronically tardy person is never early, always behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'Early' hints that the rest describes a habitually late person, the very opposite of early.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial stages are the earliest ones, so the adjective means coming at the beginning.

clue.text: Succumbing, turn in weapon to the German

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
taken as written
a gun is a weapon
der is German for 'the' (masculine)

explanation.surface: Someone giving in by surrendering their weapon to a German soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn in' reads as hand over, but it splits into a turn and the word in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overwhelmed or defeated, or to sink, is an idiom for submitting or failing.

clue.text: Straightened out West indian student in trouble

indicators.note: things in trouble are in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: WI is the abbreviation for West Indian, as for the cricket team
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Caribbean student in difficulty gets his affairs sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer coiled or kinked has been straightened, like a rope with its strands unwound.

clue.text: Offer excuse for holding party in capital

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps another inside it

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, as does 'capital!'; the 1 reads as I
Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: Someone making excuses for throwing a party in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city but is the old exclamation of approval, excellent, which A1 also means.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this word means to provide someone with a plea of having been elsewhere.

clue.text: The ultimate giveaway, to absolutely no purpose

blocks.note: first meaning: handing over everything without any payment
second meaning: in vain, with nothing achieved

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase describes giving everything away free, and idiomatically it means efforts wasted completely in vain.

clue.text: Too rude for conversion, not acceptable

indicators.note: converting something changes its form, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark too crude to be used by missionaries converting people is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word, but its letters join the fodder; the signal is 'conversion' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is out of line or improper is colloquially described by this phrase, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Is it common for a painting to be so labelled?

definitions.text: Is it common for a painting to be so labelled?

blocks.clueFragment: Is it common for a painting to be so labelled
blocks.note: surface reading: is it usual for a picture to carry a label saying it has no name?
setter's reading: a commoner has no aristocratic rank, so the word for lacking a rank also labels a nameless picture

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is usual for a painting to be left without a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like 'usual', but it means not of noble birth, someone without a peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting with no name is labelled this way in catalogues, and a commoner lacks any noble rank such as lord.

clue.text: Orientals in temporary homes found alternative accommodation

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the dwellings named next

blocks.note: tents are temporary homes for campers
E for east plus MEN, so eastern men

explanation.surface: Easterners living in makeshift camps were rehoused elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Large blocks of rented flats, often crowded, are an alternative to living under canvas.

clue.text: Plant material from river Dickensian heroine brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the heroine's name is read from end to start

blocks.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
Little Nell, heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: Botanical matter gathered from a river where a Dickens heroine was rescued.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine powdery grains produced by flowers' anthers, carried by bees, are a botanical substance.

clue.text: Stately dance of Bedouin, say, in part of desert

indicators.note: in means the nomad goes inside the stretch of desert

blocks.note: sand makes up much of a desert
a Bedouin is an example of an Arab, hence 'say'

explanation.surface: A slow dignified dance performed by nomads somewhere in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: This slow solemn Spanish court dance in triple time also became a movement in Baroque suites.

clue.text: Make sick with mouldy leftover

blocks.note: food gone mouldy has gone off
an end is a leftover scrap, like a candle end

explanation.surface: Eating stale mouldy leftovers makes you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgust or sicken someone, as a smell can, is to upset their sensibilities.

clue.text: Enthusiast getting prize for tree

blocks.note: a fan is an enthusiast
the palm is a symbol of victory, hence a prize, as in 'bear the palm'

explanation.surface: A keen supporter wins a trophy for a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm with leaves spread like an opened fan is a kind of tropical tree.

clue.text: Support a revolutionary in pain

blocks.note: to back is to support
taken as written
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: Backing a revolutionary cause in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the lumbar region is a particular kind of physical suffering or discomfort.

clue.text: Business at one time in credit needs new start

indicators.note: in means the time phrase goes inside the abbreviation for credit
start means we keep only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
once means formerly
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A company once in good financial standing needs a fresh beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or commercial enterprise is called a going one of these, a noun for a company.

clue.text: Deity bringing a point to lives

blocks.note: taken as written
the nub is the central point of a matter
to live is to be, so 'lives' gives 'is'

explanation.surface: A god giving meaning to people's lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal-headed Egyptian god of the dead and embalming is one of ancient Egypt's gods.

clue.text: Cite religious work in speech by way of embellishment

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the formal speech

blocks.note: an oration is a formal speech
to cite someone is to name them
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Quoting scripture in a sermon to decorate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoration added to make something more elaborate, as in architecture or music, is this kind of adornment.

clue.text: Language of people I had encountered on island

blocks.note: I'd is short for I had
IOM is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: The speech of people I met on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner of expression peculiar to a particular group or region is its distinctive way of speaking.

clue.text: Stoppage said to be result of political alliance

indicators.note: said means we go by what is heard rather than by spelling

blocks.note: a block is an obstruction or stoppage

explanation.surface: An obstruction reportedly caused by a coalition of parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nations or parties combining for a common purpose, like the old Soviet one, forms a grouping.

clue.text: Pulled out, being fatigued

blocks.note: first meaning: extracted, as a sword or a tooth
second meaning: haggard and tired-looking

explanation.surface: Someone withdrawn from an event because exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword taken from its sheath has been extracted, and a tired face looks pinched and haggard.

clue.text: Perfect excellence admirer and I share

blocks.note: a beau is a male admirer
taken as written
to deal is to share out, as cards

explanation.surface: A suitor and I divide up something flawless between us.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means the highest standard of perfection, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Old king is totally destructive about me

indicators.note: about means the destroying word goes around the next piece

blocks.note: rases, a variant of razes, means destroys completely
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch rampaging destructively around the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Rase is an older spelling of raze, to level to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Egyptian pharaohs bore this name, most famously the second, so it names an ancient ruler.

clue.text: Fiendish protest devil cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the devil's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
Old Nick is the Devil

explanation.surface: A wild protest where the devil is cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish or diabolical behaviour is like that of an evil spirit from hell.
